plays.name: Compared To What
plays.thesis: Turns a price objection into a comparison the rep can actually win by making the buyer name their alternative.
plays.when_to_use: When the buyer has described the problem but has not yet felt what it costs them.
beats: Describe a comparable situation, not your product
Hand the frame back with a question

segments.text: Thanks both. Marcus, Ayesha will have given you the short version, but I would rather you heard the number from your own data than from me. Can I put the model up?

Please do. And I will say up front so we do not waste each other's time, I am sceptical about platforms generally. We have bought two in three years that nobody uses. One of them we are still paying for. So the bar here is not whether the product is good, it is whether it changes what people actually do on a Tuesday.
That is fair, and I would rather hear it now than in six months. What happened with those two?

Both the same story, more or less. They were sold to me, I got excited, we rolled them out to a team that had not asked for anything, and within about four months everyone had drifted back to what they were doing before. The tooling was fine. The problem was that nobody had established what it was replacing, so it became an extra thing rather than a different thing. That is on me as much as the vendors.

Then let me be careful about how I answer the rest of this, because I do not want to be the third. On the model: four hundred contracts, average uplift seven percent, average value roughly one hundred and thirty thousand. Four missed renewals last quarter, which at your own numbers is about thirty six thousand of uplift gone.

That number is roughly right. I would want to look at whether last quarter was typical before I annualise it, because November is genuinely our worst month for coverage and it may be flattering the case. But even if you halve it, it is not a small number.
Halve it and it is seventy two thousand a year. The platform is fifty two.

Which is still a lot for what is, at some level, a spreadsheet replacement. Honestly, that price is high for us. We are not a huge business and fifty two thousand of committed annual spend is a real decision, not a rounding error.
Compared to what, though? Genuinely, I want to know what you are comparing it to, because that changes my answer.

Compared to hiring another coordinator. Fully loaded that is about forty thousand, and I get a person who can do other things when renewals are quiet. That is the alternative that keeps occurring to me and I have not been able to talk myself out of it.

That is a good comparison and I am not going to dismiss it. Can I push on it for a second? The coordinator you have is excellent, and the four you lost were lost while she was doing her job well, because she was on leave. A second coordinator halves that risk. It does not remove it, and it adds a handover between two people.

No, that is fair, and the handover is genuinely where things go wrong for us. We have seen that in other parts of the business. Two people covering something is often worse than one, because each assumes the other has it. I had not thought about it in those terms but you are right that hiring does not actually solve the failure mode I described, it just makes it less frequent.

So the way I would frame it, and you should push back if this is convenient reasoning on my part, is that the coordinator is forty thousand to reduce the risk, and this is fifty two to remove the dependency on anyone remembering at all. If it recovers even two of the four, it has paid for itself, and you still have your coordinator doing the work she was actually hired for.

Two of four is not a high bar. That is the part that makes this difficult to argue against, and I notice I am looking for a reason to say no rather than evaluating it. Let me ask Ayesha something instead. Would the ops team actually use this, or am I about to buy platform number three?

They would use it if it replaced the spreadsheet rather than sitting next to it. That is the whole thing for me. If in three months both exist, we have failed, and I would want to be able to say that out loud rather than pretending it is going fine.
Then that is the condition I would want written into the rollout. If ninety days in the spreadsheet still exists, we have failed, and you should tell us so.
I would like that in writing, not as a handshake. Put it in the contract as a success criterion and I will take this to procurement on Monday.
I will put it in the proposal as a success criterion rather than a footnote. Marcus, what is the process from there on your side?

Legal and procurement together, about two weeks if nothing is contentious. I can start that in parallel with the commercial conversation if we are broadly agreed on the number, which I think we are. The one thing I will not do is compress legal, so if you need this signed by month end that is not going to happen and I would rather say so now.
Understood, and I would rather have it right than fast. Can I send the proposal tomorrow morning, and can you and I speak Friday to close out any changes so procurement starts Monday?
Friday morning works. Ayesha, you should be on that too.
I will send the invite for Friday at ten and the proposal by nine tomorrow. Thank you both.
